a_rows_sample.anchor: primitive inputs ──①──► assertion/proposition ──②──► knowledge state ──③──► transformation ──④──► resulting state ──⑤──► invariants ──⑥──► assessment/validation ──⑦──► governance/authority ──⑧──► observable evidence ... Six of eight arrows are closed and executed. The chain breaks at ⑥.
a_rows_sample.statement: An eight-arrow dependency chain from primitive inputs to observable evidence is interrogated arrow by arrow: arrows 1-5 (proposition/assertion typing, knowledge-state construction, transformation signature, resulting-state closure/determinism/congruence, invariants) are YES/executed; arrow 6 (Assessment with Policy semantics) is NO (gap G-2); arrow 7 (governance/authority) is YES for the Gamma value set but only partially modeled for authority; arrow 8 (observation-to-evidence qualification) is PARTIAL (gap G-4) — six of eight arrows are closed and executed, and the chain breaks precisely at Assessment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-1 | What is Σ? | a signed ordinal scale, or Q14's vector, or neither | ... OPEN — both candidates refuted on different axes ... BLOCKING
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-1 (BLOCKING): the formal shape of epistemic status Sigma is undetermined — both the signed-ordinal-scale candidate and Q14's five-dimensional vector candidate have been refuted on different axes; status is derived on every read, so the wrong shape corrupts every assessment; resolution route is to derive it from a policy-parameterised assessment once G-2 closes, tested by a 10-case audit re-run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-2 | What is a Policy, formally? | Policy as a mathematical object: how it maps an evidence set to a support level | Assessment is well-typed but uncomputable without it; G-1 depends on it ... knowledge-schema.yaml IS an executing policy — a model exists ... BLOCKING
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-2 (BLOCKING, and the root blocker): Policy has no formal mathematical definition (how it maps an evidence set to a support level), leaving Assessment well-typed but uncomputable, and G-1 depends on it; the running EKP's knowledge-schema.yaml is noted to already BE an executing policy, giving an existing model to generalise from; resolution route is generalising from the EKP's schema-as-policy, tested by running assessment under at least two policies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-3 | What is uncertainty? | a representation; no (Ω,ℱ,P) in 1468 files | step 246 asserts KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution with no measurable space ... OPEN — leaning DROP
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-3 (not blocking): no measure-theoretic uncertainty representation (Omega,F,P) exists anywhere across 1468 files despite step 246 asserting 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution'; step 199.19 rules out a scalar representation; Sigma already works without it; verdict leans toward DROPPING the probabilistic claim unless a derivation of (Omega,F,P) is produced, with an ordinal scale possibly sufficing instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-4 | When does an observation become evidence? | the qualification predicate in Evidence = QualifiedObservation | 253 names the concept; nothing says what qualifies ... EvidenceSet (other BC) requires non-blank, non-duplicate refs — a partial rule ... OPEN
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-4 (not blocking): step 253 names Evidence=QualifiedObservation but never specifies the qualification predicate itself; a separate bounded context's EvidenceSet independently supplies a partial rule (non-blank, non-duplicate references); resolution route is deriving the full predicate from the EKP plus EvidenceSet's discipline, tested by injecting an unqualified observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-5 | Is Q (epistemic qualification) inside K? | a decision procedure between two consistent normalisations | Claude derives external; step 253 puts it inside ... falsifier exists: does stored status diverge from recomputed? ... OPEN — genuinely undecided
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-5 (not blocking, but flagged as the one candidate that may become genuinely normative): whether epistemic qualification Q belongs inside K has two mutually consistent normalisations (one external-derivation model, step 253's inside-K model) with no decision procedure between them; a concrete falsifier exists (does stored status ever diverge from recomputed status?), so it is treated as an empirical question first, deferred to artifact I test 12 rather than escalated to the human prematurely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-6 | Acyclicity of supersedes | none — theorem proven; implementation does not enforce it | a cycle makes "which is current?" undefined ... EKP circular_dependency is a warning over requires/depends_on only ... PROVEN ... NOT CONFORMANT ... ACTIONABLE ENGINEERING FIX
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-6 (not blocking, but an ACTIONABLE ENGINEERING FIX): the acyclicity-of-supersedes theorem is PROVEN, but the EKP's circular_dependency check is only a warning scoped to requires/depends_on, leaving supersession cycles unenforced (currently vacuous, 0 edges); resolution is to extend the lint rule and raise its severity, tested by closing a supersession cycle and re-running lint.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-7 | retract breaks F∘T̂ = T∘F | either exclude retract or add tombstones | step 254's own adequacy criterion fails on one operation ... adopt append-only (matches ReplayAssertion's immutability invariant) ... OPEN — recommend append-only
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-7 (not blocking): the retract operation is found to break step 254's own commuting-square adequacy criterion F-compose-That = T-compose-F, evidenced by both a corpus citation (step 254) and an independently executed cascade-lossiness demonstration; the recommended resolution is to adopt an append-only model with tombstones (matching a separate ReplayAssertion immutability invariant) rather than excluding retract outright, tested by a commuting-square test specifically on retract.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-8 | ~500 invariant IDs, zero crosswalks | a crosswalk | the corpus's invariants are unreconciled with the 18 executable ones ... my own standing gap G2 ... OPEN — verifier's own debt
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-8 (not blocking, explicitly the verifier's own debt): roughly 500 corpus invariant IDs remain uncrosswalked against the EKP's 18 executable lint rules; no crosswalk attempt has yet been made.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G-9 | E/V symbol collision | disambiguation | E=Entity/Events, V=Value/Vertices ... OPEN — terminology
a_rows_sample.statement: Gap G-9 (not blocking, terminology only): the E (Entity/Events) and V (Value/Vertices) symbol collisions identified earlier in the programme remain open, with the resolution route being a rename in the canonical vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CB-1 Assurance contradictory -> CLOSED — split into JustificationStrength / Traceability / Risk / GovernanceValid (artifact B) ... CB-2 P=(E,D,V) undefined -> CLOSED — Entity/Dimension/Value, Q14 ... CB-4 theory disconnected from EKP -> CLOSED — triangulated; 7 predicates engineeringally verified ..
a_rows_sample.statement: Four previously-open corpus gaps (CB-series) are recorded CLOSED as of this phase: CB-1 (Assurance's internal contradiction, closed by the four-way split), CB-2 (P=(E,D,V) undefined, closed by the Entity/Dimension/Value resolution), CB-4 (theory disconnected from the EKP, closed by triangulation with 7 engineeringally verified predicates), and CB-7 (the state/history boundary, closed as SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: None are put to you. For each candidate I performed the five required attempts ... I am asking you nothing this phase. Every open item has a derivation route or a test that has not yet been attempted.
a_rows_sample.statement: Normative-decision discipline: no gap is escalated to the human this phase; G-1/G-2 are judged not normative (G-2 is derivable from the EKP's schema-as-policy, and G-1 follows once G-2 closes), G-3 is not yet normative (evidence leans against the probabilistic reading but a derivation could still refute it outright), G-5 is the only candidate that MAY become genuinely normative but has an empirical falsifier that must be tried first, and G-6 is a proven-theorem engineering fix, not a choice — every open item has an untried derivation route or test, so nothing is asked of the human yet.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMALLY INCOMPLETE. Not FORMALLY INCONSISTENT: no contradiction survives ... Not FORMALLY CLOSED: constructed ✓ instantiated ✓ transformed ✓ compared ✓ checked for validity ✓ — but ASSESSED ✗. Assessment is well-typed and uncomputable, because Policy is undefined (G-2) ... No circular definitions r
a_rows_sample.statement: Final decision-gate verdict on whether the theory can be constructed/instantiated/transformed/compared/assessed/checked without undefined objects or circularity: FORMALLY INCOMPLETE — explicitly not FORMALLY INCONSISTENT (the Assurance self-reference was split, not carried as a contradiction; the Sigma bidirectional refutation is held open, not inconsistent) and not fully closed either, because five of six required capabilities succeed (construct/instantiate/transform/compare/validity-check) but Assessment fails, being well-typed yet uncomputable while Policy (G-2) remains undefined; the dependency graph is re-verified acyclic (Sigma derives from Assessment never from K; contradicts reads but does not write R; Valid is purely structural); every other foundational object (P, Entity, Dimension, Value, Evidence, Assertion, K, T, History, Gamma) is defined — Policy is explicitly named the single last undefined foundational object and the one that blocks.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PARTIALLY ENGINEERINGALLY CONFORMANT. 7 predicates enforced and executed · 1 non-conformant (unguarded acyclicity, G-6) · 6 absent · 3 implementation invariants exceed the theory. The two verdicts are deliberately not collapsed: the theory is more complete mathematically than the EKP implements, and
a_rows_sample.statement: Second final-gate verdict, on empirical conformance: PARTIALLY ENGINEERINGALLY CONFORMANT; the mathematical-completeness verdict (FORMALLY INCOMPLETE) and the engineering-conformance verdict are deliberately kept separate and not collapsed into one score, since the theory is mathematically more complete than the EKP implements, while the EKP enforces more governance invariants than the theory currently has — neither representation dominates the other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A measurement is a homomorphism f:Ω→ℝ or into another numerical representation that preserves the relevant relational structure. Thus Measurement ≠ Value. A Value can exist in KnowledgeOS without being a numerical measurement. ... prevents the theory from making the earlier dangerous leap: Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Representation-theorem principle: a measurement is a structure-preserving homomorphism from a relational system into a numerical (or other) representation, so Measurement != Value — a KnowledgeOS Value can exist without being a numerical measurement at all; this directly blocks the earlier dangerous claim 'KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution', already separately contested (gap G-3) because no underlying probability space (Omega,F,P) exists in the corpus.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the surviving strength component is ordinal and explicitly states: no interval structure exists for that strength dimension; consequently averaging, summing, or weighted confidence combination is not admissible. ... an operation such as (Strength1+Strength2)/2 cannot simply be introduced because it
a_rows_sample.statement: Direct, load-bearing consequence for the epistemic-status gap (G-1): since the audit's surviving epistemic 'strength' component is ordinal with no interval structure, averaging, summing, or weighted combination of strength values (e.g. (Strength1+Strength2)/2) is formally inadmissible regardless of computational convenience — the scale semantics, not ease of implementation, must authorize any such operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VALUE-SPACE SEMANTICS: SUBSTANTIALLY ESTABLISHED. ... Type(D)→Φ_D→Meaningfulness_D→AllowedOperations_D. ... Q14's classification of Version as Interval should not currently be promoted as mathematically valid. ... the theory's remaining blockers are now Σ, Assurance, Uncertainty, and Assessment/poli
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 264 verdict: VALUE-SPACE SEMANTICS SUBSTANTIALLY ESTABLISHED, with the mathematical chain Type(D) -> admissible transformations Phi_D -> Meaningfulness_D -> AllowedOperations_D as the central result; the corrective note that Version-as-Interval should not be promoted as mathematically valid is retained; the broader audit is cited as identifying the theory's remaining blockers as Sigma, Assurance, Uncertainty, and Assessment/policy semantics — no longer the basic P=(E,D,V) construction, which is now considered essentially settled.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy : K × Context → Criterion | REJECTED — makes a policy state-dependent ... Policy : Observation → Decision | REJECTED — skips proposition, evidence and authority; conflates policy with decision ... Policy : Claim × Evidence × Context → Assessment | REJECTED as the TYPE — this is the signature
a_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate Policy signatures are eliminated with executed reasoning: Policy:K x Context->Criterion is rejected because it makes policy state-dependent and unversionable/unauditable; Policy:Observation->Decision is rejected for skipping proposition/evidence/authority and conflating policy with decision (already refuted at corpus steps 202/206); Policy:Claim x Evidence x Context->Assessment is rejected as confusing Policy with Assessment's own signature (Assessment takes a Policy as a parameter); and 'Policy = a set of predicates' is subsumed by (not wrong, just incomplete versus) the Rules component, since it omits temporal applicability and unknown-handling.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy = (id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior) ... Gates : SET of three-valued predicates g : Decision → {True, False, Unknown} ... a_rows_sample.statement: The derived canonical Policy type: Policy=(id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior), where Gates is a set of three-valued predicates over a Decision, ValidityInterval is a half-open temporal window, and ResolutionBehavior maps Unknown to Block or Allow; the Apply function is a strict three-valued conjunction over Gates (False if any gate is False, ResolutionBehavior(Unknown) if any gate is Unknown and none is False, True otherwise, with no averaging), and Applicable(p,t) checks temporal membership in the validity interval — this directly answers gap G-2.

a_rows_sample.statement: Executes exec/t285_reconcile.py T-E with two concrete operations o1 (Assert a2, origin:scan, actor:tool) and o2 (Assert a2, origin:vendor, actor:human) starting from state K0=['a1']: both produce resulting state ['a1','a2'] (states equal) while the operations themselves differ (operations equal=False). Confirmed and required: collapsing the two operations would make 'who asserted this, on whose authority' unrecoverable from the state — an outcome the estate has already suffered once (two authority acts sharing one grantId, a silent loss of an authority act, per implementation evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Under the verification lane's own identity rule `id = H(P, e, c, t, Π)`, **`Π` is inside the hash.** So `o₁` and `o₂` produce assertions with *different ids*, hence **structurally different states**, and the antecedent `δ(K,o₁) = δ(K,o₂)` is **false** — the property never fires. **It fires only under semantic equality**
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows the property is equality-relative: under structural equality (id=H(P,e,c,t,Π), which includes provenance Π) o1 and o2 produce different ids, so the antecedent is false and the property never fires — vacuously true and useless under structural equality, required and load-bearing under semantic equality, and required under observational equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Typed result:** `δ(K,o₁) =_semantic δ(K,o₂) ⇏ o₁ = o₂`. **Stating the property without naming the equality makes it vacuous.** ... the Gītā framing — *"do not define the action by its fruit"* — does not by itself supply the qualification. **Philosophy asked the question; the equality typing answered it.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final typed result: delta(K,o1)=semantic delta(K,o2) does not imply o1=o2, and stating it without naming the equality relation makes it vacuous; the Gita's framing ('do not define the action by its fruit') does not by itself supply this qualification — philosophy asked the question, the equality typing methodology answered it.

b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes an operation/action o from its state consequence δ(K,o), the resulting state K', and the resulting history H' as four potentially separate formal objects, arguing operations must not be defined merely as 'the state change they cause'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: δ(K,o_1)=K' and δ(K,o_2)=K' ... o_1 ≠ o_2 may still be necessary ... δ(K,o_1)=δ(K,o_2) ⇏ o_1=o_2 ... Two different operations can produce observationally equivalent states while having different provenance; authority; evidence; history; lineage; governance meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central hypothesis of the non-injectivity object: the transition function δ may map two distinct operations to the same resulting state while those operations remain distinguishable by provenance/authority/evidence/history/lineage/governance meaning; named explicitly as 'a major research question for KnowledgeOS', not asserted as settled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: δ(K,o_1)=K' and δ(K,o_2)=K' does not imply o_1=o_2. Therefore δ(K,o_1)=δ(K,o_2) ⇏ o_1=o_2. This is a legitimate mathematical proposition to investigate. The Gītā provides philosophical corroboration, not the proof.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the operation-non-injectivity hypothesis (δ need not be injective in its operation argument) already found in the sibling document (S2055), here with the explicit epistemic qualifier that the Gita's action/result distinction merely corroborates the proposition philosophically rather than proving it mathematically.

b_rows_sample.statement: T-E confirms the operation-non-injectivity hypothesis (delta(K,o1)=delta(K,o2) does not imply o1=o2) with a worked example (two Assert operations with the same target assertion but different origin/actor provenance), but sharpens it into a typed result: the non-injectivity property holds only under SEMANTIC equality of states (ignoring identity/provenance fields) -- under STRUCTURAL equality (where identity hashes provenance Pi), the two resulting states are not actually equal either, so the property would be vacuous under that equality notion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action is not optional. The system must act. But action without attachment to results is the path to liberation (Decision Readiness).
a_rows_sample.statement: Central thesis: KnowledgeOS cannot merely observe — Transformation T is mandatory — but T must be performed without attachment to whether it achieves EC=TRUE (Decision Readiness) in order to reach liberation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = δ(K_t, e_t) is mandatory ... The system cannot simply observe; it must transform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues, from 'no one can abstain from action even for a single moment' (Gita 3.3-5), that the KnowledgeOS state-transition function δ is mandatory — i.e. the system architecture cannot have a pure-observation-only mode.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Non-attachment ≠ Inaction ... True renunciation = Action without attachment
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws an explicit distinction between non-attachment and inaction, arguing (from the 'hypocrisy of inaction' verses 3.6-7) that a system which merely observes while internally desiring an outcome is worse ('hypocrite') than one that acts but without attachment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system acts even when EC = TRUE because others depend on it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives, from Krishna's argument that leaders must act by example even with nothing to gain (3.20-24, King Janak), a KnowledgeOS governance claim that the system should continue acting/transforming even after reaching Decision Readiness (EC=TRUE), because other dependent users/processes follow its example — an argument for continued action grounded in social/systemic responsibility rather than the system's own evidentiary need.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Wise(T) = T with Attachment(T) = 0 ... Desire = Attachment to EC = TRUE ... To attain Decision Readiness, eliminate desire.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the wise/ignorant distinction purely in terms of the Attachment(T) predicate, and separately claims desire is identical to attachment to the specific outcome EC=TRUE, concluding that eliminating desire is necessary to attain Decision Readiness — an unproven necessity claim (only sufficiency was argued via the Gita analogy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: T(K_t) = Action according to N_t without attachment to EC ... KnowledgeOS = Action + Duty + Detachment + Feedback + Wisdom
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the chapter's five derived principles (action mandatory, duty defines action, non-attachment liberates, eternal observe-transform-observe cycle, desire covers knowledge) into a single closing additive equation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Tripuisi model: Jnata (Knower) / Jnana (Knowing) / Jneya (Known). This provides one of the strongest conceptual models.
a_rows_sample.statement: Vedanta Tripuisi lens: Knower / Knowing / Known (Jnata / Jnana / Jneya) is described as one of the strongest conceptual models surfaced so far for KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Krishna** | Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens | $L: \Omega \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ |
a_rows_sample.statement: A nine-row core correspondence table maps Gita concepts to KnowledgeOS concepts and formal notation: Krishna -> Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens (L: Omega -> P(Omega)); Arjuna -> the Knower (Actor State A_t); Wisdom/Jnana -> Knowledge State K_t; Action/Karma -> Epistemic Action/Assertion (a_t in A); Doubt/Samsaya -> Gap/Discrepancy (Delta_t); Faith/Sraddha -> Epistemic Trust/Policy (rho); Teacher/Guru -> Source/Evidence (S in S); Liberation/Moksa -> Decision Readiness (DR_t = 1); Attachment/Raga -> Epistemic Bias (b: K_t -> K_t').

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can give us additional architectural insight, but we should derive it as a set of architectural principles and testable hypotheses—not copy theological statements into the architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: The central methodological rule for using Chapter 4 (and by extension any external/theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input: derive architectural principles and testable hypotheses from the source, never copy theological statements directly into the architecture. Nine principles are derived under this discipline: (1) knowledge has lineage -- K_t should conceptually be (content, provenance, status, history), not a bare object, though this equation is explicitly withheld from v0.2 pending testing; (2) loss of knowledge is not the same as invalid knowledge (NOT KNOWN NOW != NEVER KNOWN; CURRENTLY UNAVAILABLE != FALSE), supporting layered epistemic state without determining the exact state algebra; (3) state continuity can exist without state memory (continuity != memory != observability), suggesting a distinction between current state, historical continuity, accessible history, and authoritative history, classified [LENS]/[HYPOTHESIS] not ratified architecture; (4) condition-triggered intervention (a governance trigger pattern: Guard(s)=true => Remediation(s)), with the explicit warning not to jump from the narrative directly to an architecture rule -- test whether KnowledgeOS already contains the same structural pattern first; (5) action, inaction, and forbidden action are different states (not a Boolean), informing the open question OQ-4 via Execution != Consequence and ObservedActivity != ActionSemantics; (6) knowledge changes the meaning of action (MeaningOfAction(x | KnowledgeState), i.e. action is context-dependent, not semantically isolated); (7) knowledge acquisition has a protocol (a governed relationship of trust/inquiry/transformation, reinforcing an existing Extraction != Determination finding, R1); (8) doubt should be a first-class object (Doubt_t = f(K_t, Evidence_t, Contradiction_t, Requirement_t), explicitly marked as a research hypothesis, not to be added to the architecture yet); (9) knowledge and action form a closed loop (K_t -> Z_t -> Proposal -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Observation -> K_{t+1}), used as a comparative validation lens for an already-existing loop rather than as new architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna → Lord Lens ... That's too strong. A safer mapping is: Gītā concept → structural property → abstract pattern → possible KnowledgeOS correspondence
a_rows_sample.statement: S1321's direct character-to-variable mappings (Krishna -> Lord Lens, Arjuna -> Knower, made at the very beginning of that document) are judged too strong a jump from theological/metaphysical claim straight to software variable, skipping an intermediate abstraction level. A safer four-step mapping discipline is proposed: Gita concept -> structural property (observed in text) -> abstract pattern (generalized) -> possible KnowledgeOS correspondence (candidate) -- rather than Gita concept -> mathematical equation -> KnowledgeOS architecture directly. Example: Krishna's intentional manifestation does not directly imply 'Lord = generator operator'; instead, 'the narrative distinguishes an agent that knowingly intervenes under a purpose and condition,' studied as a structural analogue of purpose-conditioned intervention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 4 can function as an **independent stress-test lens**. That is more valuable than trying to make it a source of architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes going one step further than the corrective ruling: rather than treating Chapter 4 as failing to derive the architecture, use it as an independent stress-test lens, pairing eight existing KnowledgeOS concepts with a Chapter-4-derived stress question each: K_t (can state continuity exist without complete memory?); X_t != Observed(X_t) (can history exist without present observability?); Evidence (can multiple transmission paths remain distinguishable?); Determination (what transforms transmitted information into accepted knowledge?); Authorization (what distinguishes knowing an action from being entitled to perform it?); Action (is action semantics independent of physical execution?); Governance (what triggers intervention when the current state diverges from intended order?); OQ-4 (can execution/consequence be modelled separately from action intent?). This use is judged stronger than treating the text as either a source of architecture or a failed derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not ask: "What KnowledgeOS object corresponds to Krishna, Arjuna, Guru, etc.?" We should ask: **"What philosophical principle is expressed here, and what does that principle teach us about KnowledgeOS?"**
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a five-step philosophical interpretation method for using Chapter 4 (or any theological source) as KnowledgeOS research input, replacing character-to-object mapping: (1) extract the philosophical principle, not names/mythology/literal narrative (e.g. 'knowledge should produce discrimination between action and non-action'); (2) generalize the principle, removing Gita-specific theological context while preserving the underlying idea (e.g. 'a knowledge-bearing system needs discernment concerning possible actions'); (3) compare with KnowledgeOS, asking whether an existing mechanism already expresses the principle (e.g. K_t -> Zero -> Proposal -> Decision as a candidate correspondence); (4) stress-test it, asking a sharper question than simple mapping (e.g. does the current model really distinguish 'what can be done' from 'what should be done'); (5) classify the result into one of five outcomes: CONVERGENT (philosophy independently expresses something already present), REFINING (suggests a distinction the architecture should examine), NEW HYPOTHESIS (introduces a potentially useful concept), NOT APPLICABLE (philosophically interesting but architecturally irrelevant), or CONTRASTING (the philosophical principle exposes a tension with the current model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 1: THE CRISIS ... Chapter 2: THE FRAME ... Chapter 3: THE ACTION SYSTEM ... Chapter 4: THE KNOWLEDGE-ACTION TRANSFORMATION ... This sequence suggests that a KnowledgeOS system should begin with: Problem → Purpose → Knowledge Requirement, not: Data → Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally accepts a shift from 'mapping' (what Gita concept maps to what KnowledgeOS object) to 'testing' (what theory of knowledge/action/decision/responsibility/state/transformation emerges from the text, tested against the architecture). Chapters 1-4 are read as a coherent progression mirroring the KnowledgeOS lifecycle: Chapter 1 the crisis ('I do not know what I should do'), Chapter 2 the frame (nature of self/duty/knowledge/disciplined action), Chapter 3 the action system (interdependence/duty/consequence/responsibility), Chapter 4 the knowledge-action transformation (how knowledge changes the meaning and consequence of action). This progression is read as suggesting a KnowledgeOS system should begin with Problem -> Purpose -> Knowledge Requirement rather than Data -> Knowledge, strengthening the existing architecture's roles (Knower=entity with a problem, Purpose=what must be determined, IdealState=what would constitute resolution, KnowledgeState=what is currently known, Zero=what remains unresolved, Lord=what might be relevant, Sarathi=what action follows).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 16 work-item records hold 210 transitions and 99 grants... The records store NO derived state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten measured observations (O-1..O-10) about the estate's runtime governance store: .gitignore excludes the whole of .claude/runtime; 16 records hold 210 transitions/99 grants; the records persist only an append-only evidence log and authority record, never derived state (mutationOwner, sessions, workItemState are fold-computed and never stored); seq is dense/monotonic in every record; only 2 of 210 transitions carry any date field; reconstructability from tracked documents measures 100% for sessions and 83% for grants, with the 16 uncited grants overwhelmingly amendments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The load-bearing observation: there is no runtime state in the runtime directory... the artifact under runtime/ is not runtime state. It is governance evidence that happens to be stored in a runtime location.
a_rows_sample.statement: The reframing that changes the question: the problem is not whether runtime state should be tracked (there is no runtime execution state to track), but that governance evidence has been misfiled into a runtime location whose gitignore contract is correct for the location and wrong for the content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option A — track .claude/runtime/ directly ... Option B — governance snapshot model ... Option C — runtime-only
a_rows_sample.statement: Three options are analysed for durable governance state: A (track runtime directly — risks a JSON-array merge-conflict class, mitigated but not removed by dense/monotonic seq gap-detection); B (governance snapshot export — risks a second representation and divergence, and the snapshot must be mechanical, never an act, to avoid Governance preserving its own authority record); C (status quo, runtime-only — measured 100%/83% reconstructable, but the lossy layer is precisely the amendment layer, the load-bearing constraints).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: Option B′ — RELOCATION, which is Option B with the boundary set at the SOURCE rather than at an export.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends relocating the authority record out of runtime/ into a tracked, append-only governance-evidence location (Option B'), reasoned as dominating A (avoids the merge-conflict class inherent to a directory contracted as ephemeral) and B (has exactly one representation, avoiding the anti-corruption/divergence problem) and C (does not leave the amendment layer outside durable history); flags this recommendation as a variant beyond the three commissioned options.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O-7 has a migration consequence worth stating precisely: the log has almost no time dimension... Do not let an import be mistaken for a chronology.
a_rows_sample.statement: M-3: because only 2 of 210 transitions carry a date field, importing the record into git would make commit times the only available time evidence, and those would be import times, not act times; this is a pre-existing gap, not one relocation creates, but relocation must not let an import commit be mistaken for a chronology.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision authority is reserved to the human PO/ARB... This process authored the ADR... approving this particular ADR is the single act this process is most specifically barred from.
a_rows_sample.statement: A process declines to perform the PO/ARB decision role on two independent grounds: decision authority is reserved to the human PO/ARB (a process writing 'DECIDED' would manufacture authority, not record it), and this specific process authored the ADR under decision, so approving it is the one act it is most specifically barred from.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture proposal → Principal Architect recommendation → PO/ARB decision → Governance registration
a_rows_sample.statement: A four-stage authority chain is stated compactly by the PO/ARB themselves as the reason a recommendation must not be read as a decision: Architecture proposal → Principal Architect recommendation → PO/ARB decision → Governance registration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: commit de998173 (2026-08-19) committed the narrative lineage — sixteen review documents — while all 28 grants and 33 transitions remained outside git
a_rows_sample.statement: First-hand, dated, reproducible evidence of Option C's failure mode: a specific commit durably preserved sixteen narrative review documents while all 28 grants and 33 transitions of the underlying authority record remained outside git — documents survived, the record they register against did not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The business value is actually not 'moving files from .claude/runtime to another directory'... The real business value is that the organization gains a trustworthy engineering governance memory.
a_rows_sample.statement: A narrative business-value case restating the ADR/decision's technical content across six dimensions (auditability/compliance, reduced operational risk, faster engineering decisions, prevention of expensive architecture drift, responsible AI-assisted engineering, IP protection, reduced cost of disagreement).

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-11: the Governance review is completeness, provenance, amendment lineage and current/superseded document integrity, and IS NOT technical Architecture verification, design-soundness verification or migration safety verification
a_rows_sample.statement: A bounded-review-scope discipline preventing a completeness-only review from being cited as technical sign-off.

a_rows_sample.anchor: verdict: CHAIN NOT READY FOR PO/ARB ACCEPTANCE -- DV-1..DV-7 and RV-1..RV-7 remain open; migration not authorized; Phase 3 must not begin
a_rows_sample.statement: A governance determination that the routed correction chain (Architecture repair -> bounded review -> PO/ARB) had not been discharged at the Architecture stage.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Repair RV-1...RV-7 only, produce evidence, stop. NOT 'continue migration.'
a_rows_sample.statement: A bounded-commission pattern in which the PO/ARB explicitly authorizes a narrow repair scope and forbids using the same authorization to widen scope toward the ultimate migration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the 18 property tests (T1-T18) all passing, with three tests explicitly re-specified mid-run to measure the property rather than the raw string (disclosed, not hidden)
a_rows_sample.statement: Documents a verification-integrity practice: when a naive string-match test would fail on the correction's own labelled-history quotations, the test is re-specified to test the underlying property, and this loosening is explicitly disclosed rather than silently applied.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the independent review's own sub-breakdown said '11 shell scripts'; the re-measured true count is 10 shell scripts (13 entries total, which was correct)
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance re-verification catching and correcting a small measurement error made by the prior independent Architecture reviewer, recorded so a future reader does not re-open the finding from the wrong sub-breakdown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Accepted for correction-chain completion. Not accepted as migration authorization. Untracked governance artifacts remain an explicit migration prerequisite.
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB's final acceptance wording, carefully scoping what closes (this correction chain's findings) versus what remains open (the durability observation itself, owned by migration preparation) so no reader can claim the durability problem is solved by this acceptance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two records disagree on whether the durability decision was made
b_rows_sample.statement: The runtime authority record (grant G-KOS-GOV-STATE-DURABILITY-DECISION) quotes a PO/ARB DECISION ACT 2026-08-19 selecting D1=B' (Governance Evidence Relocation) and D2=ADOPT (R-CONFLICT). The tracked registration review (...po-arb-position-registration.md), at its last recorded act, shows D1 NOT SELECTED, D2 NOT SELECTED, DECISION.md NOT PRODUCED. Both sides are recorded; the act sequence that moved D1/D2 from NOT SELECTED to SELECTED is UNKNOWN in the current corpus (U-3). The runtime record is the authoritative workflow state per state=fold, but the registration review is not amended to match.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the durability inversion (headline structural finding)
b_rows_sample.statement: The runtime directory -- the only gitignored .claude/ subdirectory -- holds the estate's most authoritative records (grants, transitions), while its own name says 'runtime.' There is no runtime state in the runtime directory: governance evidence is misfiled into an ephemeral, ignored location. Load-bearing DDD statement from the PO/ARB: 'An aggregate cannot depend on accidental reconstruction.' Documented consequence (commit de998173, 2026-08-19): the narrative lineage (16 review documents) was committed while all grants and transitions remained outside git.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The GOV-STATE-DURABILITY migration (B' relocation) is NOT EXECUTED, NOT AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE, MUST NOT BEGIN
b_rows_sample.statement: IMPLEMENTATION-DESIGN is PROPOSED -- DESIGN ONLY; MIGRATION-PLAN is PROPOSED, AMENDED (AMD3/4/5/6); AMD3/4/5/6 unregistered as delivered (OPEN-M6); OPEN-M1..M7 open; Phase 5 remains prohibited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Path sources are THREE, on TWO axes
b_rows_sample.statement: Where the record lives: P-1 default workflow-state.php:81, P-2 default session-resolve.php:74 (two independent defaults, RA-2), P-3a/b the two --dir overrides. Which mechanism interprets it: P-4 session-resolve.php:90 getenv('KOS_MECHANISM_PATH') -> :103 proc_open -> :156, a write-capable substitution path. The mechanism already supports relocation; only the default contradicts the B' relocation.

a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five non-equivalent senses of kernel 'minimality' (cardinality; semantic -- no operator removable without losing an irreducible capability; compositional -- every retained operator contributes something non-reproducible by composition of others; architectural -- no separate responsibility introduced when naturally derivable from another; cognitive universality -- required by every epistemic system), designating semantic+compositional minimality as the primary experimental target and cardinality as only secondary.

a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 24-item capability space (C1-C24, spanning observation acquisition, meaning construction, representation, relation, discrimination, hypothesis formation, inference, gap detection, challenge, validation, revision, inquiry-adequacy determination, action selection, context/temporal/uncertainty/assumption representation, provenance and alternative preservation, non-identifiability support, observation-vs-interpretation distinction, representation-independent semantic equivalence, smallest-adequate-answer production, and learning from new observations) that must be derived independently of the candidate operator names, not by restating them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: oi : S_i -> S_j where S_i and S_j are abstract epistemic states/artifacts. Do not assume all operators act directly on K_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes candidate operators as typed transformations over explicitly distinct carrier types (Observation, Evidence, SemanticRepresentation, Hypothesis, Model, Claim, AlternativeSet, RequirementSet, EpistemicState, DecisionProposal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every operator acts directly on K_t, and requires every proposed composite reduction o_removed=f(o_remaining) to be documented across nine dimensions (input/output type, preconditions, postconditions, semantic/epistemic effect, information loss, introduced assumptions, and whether removed semantics were secretly embedded elsewhere).

a_rows_sample.anchor: SCENARIO 7 — Missing evidence ... Expected possibility: cannot determine. ... SCENARIO 12 — Smallest adequate answer.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a 16-scenario canonical test suite grounded in concrete Nexus-infrastructure examples (basic/numeric/network observation; conflicting evidence; ambiguous semantics like 'the server is available'; temporal revision without conflating historical and current-state equality; missing evidence legitimately yielding 'cannot determine'; competing partially-supported hypotheses; model criticism; context-dependent semantic interpretation; inquiry-relative adequacy; smallest adequate answer; cost-constrained action selection; non-identifiability; provenance conflict; representation equivalence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Build a SMALL RESEARCH SIMULATOR. ... Do NOT claim this is the canonical KnowledgeOS state model. Label it: [PROP] experimental state representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires building a small, explicitly non-production research simulator over an explicitly [PROP]-labelled experimental epistemic state K_t=(claims,representations,relations,evidence,provenance,assumptions,alternatives,uncertainty,context,history), with every helper function classified (domain operator / data-structure operation / infrastructure utility / test harness / serialization) so that only genuine domain operators count toward kernel size.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Leave-one-out is not sufficient. Some operators may be individually removable but jointly necessary. ... pairwise ablation; ... selected triple ablations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires pairwise and higher-order ablation beyond simple leave-one-out, explicitly anticipating that some operators may be individually removable yet jointly necessary (synergy, substitution, hidden dependency, or operator bundles) -- illustrated by Interpret+Represent potentially being coupled without necessarily being one operator, requiring a typed factorization test rather than an assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PROPERTY P2 — Non-identifiability: If evidence cannot distinguish H1 and H2, the system must not fabricate a unique determination. ... PROPERTY P7 — No information creation: Processing existing evidence cannot create unsupported empirical information.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies ten falsifiable properties (P1-P10) for randomized property-based simulation testing: revision-representability under contradicting evidence, non-fabrication under non-identifiability, provenance preservation, temporal consistency (no erasure of historical truth), semantic distinction preserved when evidence does not resolve it, adequacy != mere answer-existence, no information creation from pure processing, alternative preservation absent evidence-based elimination, context-sensitivity of relevance, and challenge-required-before-validated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT interpret a 99% scenario success rate as proof of correctness. ... Statistics support robustness assessment; they do not prove minimality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes disciplined statistical treatment: separate deterministic logical failures from stochastic/implementation/model-specification/conceptual failures, report failure rates and robustness across seeds and sensitivity to definitional choices rather than a single aggregate score, and explicitly distinguishes the statistical robustness question (p_hat_failure) from the logical necessity question (exists x: Reach(S,x) != Reach(S union {o},x)) -- statistics inform robustness, they do not establish minimality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: But do NOT equate: information quantity = knowledge. ... Do NOT equate: Pi_t = K_t. ... fit != validation, regression != causality, estimation != identification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to run information-theoretic checks (data-processing inequality, sufficient representation) without equating information quantity with knowledge, probabilistic checks (Pi_t=L(X|F_t) without Pi_t=K_t) across six specified uncertainty scenarios, and a causal/model-criticism check enforcing fit!=validation, regression!=causality, estimation!=identification as three explicitly distinct failure classes a model must not conflate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = predicate ... Ideal State = state/target construct ... Inquiry = domain input ... Governance = external constraint ... Authorization = governance mechanism ... Select = decision/action mechanism. But these are hypotheses. Test them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a DDD pass over every candidate operator asking whether it is a genuine domain capability owning a distinct invariant/responsibility, or instead a policy, state predicate, or orchestration concern -- explicitly naming Zero, Ideal State, Inquiry, Governance, Authorization, and Select as operators whose kernel membership must be tested rather than assumed, offering (only as hypotheses) demotions of each to a non-operator role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not conclude: 'Operator X is necessary because the current KnowledgeOS architecture already has X.' That would be circular.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids architectural circularity as a justification for kernel membership (existing class != domain primitive; existing service != kernel operator; existing workflow != epistemic necessity), requiring the experiment to reason from domain capabilities and epistemic requirements rather than from current implementation structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 — Representation failure ... F19 — Implementation artifact ... F20 — Simulator artifact. Do not call F19/F20 kernel failures. ... Never manufacture a positive result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a twenty-category failure taxonomy (F1-F20) for classifying ablation failures, explicitly excluding implementation and simulator artifacts (F19/F20) from counting as genuine kernel failures, and mandates that negative results ('removing X did not break anything', 'no meaningful conclusion can currently be drawn') be treated as first-class, valid, and never suppressed in favor of manufactured positive findings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Search for multiple Pareto candidates. ... Do not collapse these into one arbitrary weighted score.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires searching for multiple Pareto-optimal candidate kernels (not one single smallest kernel) evaluated along nine uncollapsed axes (cardinality, semantic coverage, compositionality, coupling, interpretability, falsifiability, domain cohesion, implementation independence, evidence strength), with any weighted composite score requiring an explicit sensitivity analysis over weight choices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: find S subset-of O such that C_required subset-of Reach(S) and forall o in S: C_required not-subset-of Reach(S \ {o}). ... Reach(S) ... must be defined carefully.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes semantic minimality as a set-system reachability problem: find a minimal operator subset S such that all required capabilities are reachable by valid typed compositions of S, and no operator in S can be removed without breaking that containment -- explicitly cautioning that the Reach(S) composition function must be defined by explicit, non-arbitrary rules rather than declared to include whatever the researcher wishes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Empirically necessary ... Formally necessary ... DDD-necessary ... These can disagree. ... That is a very interesting result -- not a contradiction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three independent necessity tests (empirical: the simulator cannot run without it; formal: no valid composition of remaining operators supplies it; DDD: the responsibility is a genuinely distinct domain concept) that can legitimately disagree without contradiction, illustrated by Select potentially being computationally derivable from Determine while DDD analysis still separates epistemic determination from action selection as distinct responsibilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 01-research-question.md ... 03-capability-model.md ... 04-operator-contracts.md ... 05-operator-capability-matrix.md ... 06-composition-rules.md ... FINAL-kernel-reduction-report.md
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a fixed 18-file experimental output directory (docs/knowledgeos/research/kernel-reduction/), explicitly forbidding modification of canonical architecture documents and requiring the simulator code to be isolated in an experimental directory -- this file naming scheme directly matches several files this same batch reads (01-research-question.md, 03-capability-model.md, 04-operator-contracts.md, 05-operator-capability-matrix.md, 06-composition-rules.md), identifying this prompt as their likely originating mandate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would consider the experiment successful even if Claude concludes: 'The 13 operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because the semantic granularity of the candidate operators is unstable.' ... What is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive?
a_rows_sample.statement: Names as potentially the single most valuable possible experimental outcome a finding that the 13 candidate operators cannot yet be meaningfully minimized because their semantic granularity is itself unstable -- reframing the open research problem from 'which operator to delete' to 'what is the correct mathematical type and semantic granularity of an epistemic primitive', and explicitly allows the kernel to turn out structurally different from a flat operator set (e.g. K=(S,T,O) or K=(P,R,delta), or some operators turning out to be predicates like Zero rather than transformations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4. The operation-necessity test: a test was run -- but not the one G-67 names ... exhaustive search over all 16384 subsets ... minimal kernels: exactly two, both cardinality 13 ... under every audit reduction granted, |K_min| falls 13 -> 8 ... But the headline is self-superseded: Reachability != Epistemic adequacy ... PARTIALLY MOVED. An ablation ran, and it measured a different quantity than G-67 asks for. R_mandatory was never the input -- a 25-capability model was. ... AF-F-33 stays withdrawn and is now superseded by measured numbers from a declared model. 13 and 8 are not upgrades of my 14/18.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an executed 16384-subset kernel-reduction ablation (KR-2026-09-01) as PARTIALLY MOVING the lane's operation-necessity question: it is a genuine, careful experiment (finding two minimal 13-operator kernels, a missing Qualify power, |K_min| falling to 8 under every granted audit reduction, and 7/7 semantic-smuggling probes rejected), but it measures a different quantity than the lane's own G-67 criterion (which requires R_mandatory as input; the ablation instead used a declared 25-capability model) -- so the lane's prior withdrawal of AF-F-33 (its 14-forced/18-upper-bound claim) stays withdrawn and correct, and 13/8 are explicitly not upgrades of 14/18 since the two questions ('minimal under this capability model and algebra' vs 'forced by R_mandatory') remain distinct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the headline is self-superseded (19-directive-adoption-and-research-restructure.md): Reachability != Epistemic adequacy. 'The experiment falsified the assumption that kernel minimality can be determined independently of semantic representation.' The programme sequence becomes Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Minimality, and the kernel question moves from first to seventh in a seven-level hierarchy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the kernel-reduction ablation's own follow-up document self-supersedes its headline result by falsifying the assumption that kernel minimality can be determined independently of semantic representation (Reachability != Epistemic adequacy), restructuring the whole research programme sequence to Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Minimality and demoting the kernel-minimality question from first to seventh position in a seven-level research hierarchy.

But the reason changed, and the change is the finding: [table of 5 blockers, 2026-08-31 vs 2026-09-02] The blockers moved DOWNWARD -- from vocabulary disagreement to semantic undefinedness. A vocabulary blocker is resolved by a governance act; a semantic blocker is resolved by a derivation. The estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the central implementability readiness question (can two independent engineers implement the same kernel from current material without the research corpus?) as STILL NO, but frames the change as progress: five specific blockers are named across the 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02 snapshots, and the overall shift is that blockers moved from vocabulary disagreement (resolvable by a governance act) to semantic undefinedness (resolvable only by a derivation) -- summarized as 'the estate has traded four governance blockers for four derivation blockers', explicitly framed as real progress since derivation blockers are the kind a research lane can actually discharge.

Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)

a_rows_sample.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.
