b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 warns explicitly against 'Ownerless Invariants' (I exists but Owner(I) = empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints the same 15 invariants from Step 210 with the Owner column deleted entirely, and performs no such search -- discarding the exact data (Step 210's Owner column, with 7/15 ownerless and 5/15 shared) that would have triggered Step 212's own diagnosis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n

Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
b_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.

b_rows_sample.statement: V_i is DEFINED with 3/6 components at INPUTS_KNOWN (role-name granularity); the I1-I15 matrix is DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (names) but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (no mechanism/code/test); Assurance(I) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from numeric evaluation; S_reachable is DEFINED but conceded as the open challenge, not CONSTRUCTIBLE. b_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.13's 8-tuple statistical result A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity) is correct and genuinely good statistical practice, rarely done in architecture documents, but never carried into the matrix (which collapses all eight back into one row) and never connected to the corpus's prior statistical steps (025N, 074, 082, uncited). Correct refusals: Section 210.29 declines to scalarize Assurance (names fake precision explicitly); Section 210.27's Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof is a properly-used ordinal. Violations: Section 210.28's Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) compares assurance levels the same file declines to scale; the E_1<...<E_5 ladder (Section 210.30) is re-issued by Step 212 Section 212.6 with different rung contents and an added E_0 -- the same ordinal scale has two incompatible calibrations in the band, making any statement 'we have E_2 evidence' uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under -- a scale-integrity failure that silently corrupts later aggregation. The 15-row matrix itself carries no scale at all (purely nominal, no arithmetic attempted -- correct).

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: MIXED — strong distinctions (Architectural Principle != Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Memory/Identity/History split), weak ownership
b_rows_sample.statement: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property is exactly the right DDD-governance move; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity (Section 210.5, a foreign key proves existence not that this version was the artifact used) is a real and useful insight; Section 210.39's Memory/Identity/History separation, concluding the current domain object need not carry all history internally, is correct DDD (event sourcing / separate read model), well argued. Against this, the Owner column's category error means only 4/15 invariants have a single bounded-context owner, 7/15 are owned by a layer or pattern (which cannot be accountable), 5/15 are slash-shared, and I13/I14 are owned by 'Aggregate' -- a tactical pattern name is never the answer to 'who is accountable' in DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Core Deficiencies Identified: 1. Category Errors & Metaphor Overreach ... 2. Mathematical Inconsistencies: The algebraic operators (union, x, o) are used interchangeably and without defined signatures ... 3. Violations of Kernel Decoupling ... 4. Failure to Respect Non-Totality & Partiality ... Verdict: REJECTED IN PRESENT FORM -- REFACTORED TO STRICT KERNEL PRIMITIVES.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the YONI-ZERO LENS proposal in its original form on four grounds: anthropomorphic/mythological metaphor substituting for operational primitives; algebraic operators (union, Cartesian product, function composition) used interchangeably without disambiguated signatures; mixing of non-mutating queries, epistemic evaluations, and governance actions into monolithic 'Lens' operators, violating kernel-delta structural isolation; and assuming complete observability over 'Gaps'/'Unknown Gaps' without grounding in the established non-total EvalStatus vocabulary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Yoni Lens' -> Epistemic Generation Context (G_gen): An outer-kernel proposal engine that formulates candidate node assertions ASSERT(p) and link transitions LINK(p1,p2) ... 'Zero Lens' -> Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context (E_eval): The non-mutating analysis layer that runs EVal(K,p,Gamma), identifies partial/theory-blocked states, and triggers ISOLATE(p) when structural contradictions are detected ... 'Sarathi Lens' -> Determination Bridge Layer (Det): the decision interface mapping evaluation states, queries, and risk bounds to actionable determinations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Maps the three metaphoric 'Lenses' of the reviewed proposal onto verified Kernel v1.3 interfaces: Yoni Lens becomes an Epistemic Generation Context that proposes ASSERT/LINK candidate operations; Zero Lens becomes an Epistemic Evaluation & Isolation Context running EVal and triggering ISOLATE on detected structural contradiction; Sarathi Lens becomes the already-specified Determination Bridge Det. The three-role shape (generative proposal / boundary evaluation / decision guidance) closely parallels the corpus's earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi guidance cycle, with the generative role renamed from 'Lord' to 'Yoni'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1: Generative Expansion (Yoni Engine G): G(K_t,Q,Gamma) = {o_1,...,o_m} where o_i in {ASSERT,LINK,REVISE} ... Phase 2: State Mutation Transition (delta): K_temp = delta(K_t, o_m o ... o o_1, Gamma) ... Phase 3: Boundary & Partiality Examination (Zero Engine Z): Z(K_temp,Gamma) = {EVal(K_temp,p,Gamma) | p in V_temp}. If Phi_conflict(p)=true, K_{t+1}=delta(K_temp,ISOLATE(p),Gamma) ... Phase 4: Task Determination Bridge (Det): B_{t+1}=Det(Z(K_{t+1},Gamma),Q,Gamma). Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the refactored four-phase epistemic cycle: Generative Expansion G produces a batch of candidate O_core operations; State Mutation delta executes them monotonically; Boundary Examination Z runs EVal over every active node and applies ISOLATE wherever the structural conflict predicate Phi_conflict holds; the Determination Bridge Det then maps the post-isolation evaluation set to a boundary/gap profile B_{t+1}. The whole cycle is the function composition Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma).

a_rows_sample.anchor: test_refactored_epistemic_cycle: generate_proposals produces claim_alpha (A implies B) and claim_beta_conflict (A implies NOT B, with neg_support 0.80) ... if eval_beta.neg_support > 0.50: apply ISOLATE ... assert det_alpha.status == DETERMINED_POSITIVE and det_alpha.actionable == True ... assert det_beta.status == UNDETERMINED_CONFLICT and det_beta.actionable == False, 'Isolated conflict node leaked into actionable determination!' ... VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL: Pipeline conforms to KnowledgeOS v1.3 Kernel Specification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a passing end-to-end falsification test of the refactored cycle: the Generation engine proposes two claims, one internally conflicting (high positive AND high negative support on 'A implies NOT B'); the Zero engine detects the conflict and triggers ISOLATE; the Determination bridge then correctly yields DETERMINED_POSITIVE/actionable for the clean claim and UNDETERMINED_CONFLICT/non-actionable for the isolated one, printed as 'VERIFICATION SUCCESSFUL: Pipeline conforms to KnowledgeOS v1.3 Kernel Specification.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supervisory Action & Ratification Roadmap: 1. Metaphor Elimination: All references to 'Womb', 'Mirror', or 'Sarathi' are permanently stripped ... in favor of Epistemic Generation Engine (G), Boundary Evaluation Engine (Z), and Determination Bridge (Det). ... 3. Status Upgrade: Reclassified from [PROP] research formulation to [REFACTORED & RATIFIED FRAMEWORK MODULE]. Refactoring Complete. Unified Epistemic Cycle Integrated into KnowledgeOS Specification v1.3.
a_rows_sample.statement: Directs permanent elimination of the mythological terminology (Womb, Mirror, Sarathi) from canonical implementation specifications in favor of the operational engine names (Epistemic Generation Engine G, Boundary Evaluation Engine Z, Determination Bridge Det), and reclassifies the proposal's status from [PROP] research formulation to [REFACTORED & RATIFIED FRAMEWORK MODULE], declaring it integrated into KnowledgeOS Specification v1.3 -- another self-contained ratification act within the same authoring pass.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
b_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Unknown 
eq Absent 
eq NotApplicable 
eq NotObserved 
eq NotYetInvestigated
b_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

type_signature.domain: question x knowledge state x ideal state x context

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

a_notations: Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma)
a_aliases: Comprehensive Architectural Audit of the Yoni-Zero Lens

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'yoni-zero-lens-proposal-audit' POSSIBLY relates to 'zero-lord-sarathi-guidance-cycle' (batch B0062). Note: An audit that rejects an external 'YONI-ZERO LENS -- THE COMPLETE EPISTEMIC CYCLE' proposal in its original metaphor-laden form (Womb/Mirror/Sarathi imagery, undisambiguated union/product/composition operators, kernel-decoupling violations, disregard for EVal's non-totality) and refactors it into a four-phase strictly-typed pipeline: Generative Expansion (Yoni Engine G, proposing ASSERT/LINK/REVISE candidate operations), State Mutation (delta), Boundary/Partiality Examination (Zero Engine Z, running EVal and triggering ISOLATE on detected Phi_conflict), and Determination Bridge (Det, yielding a boundary/gap profile). The composed cycle is Cycle(K_t,Q,Gamma) = (Det o Z o delta o G)(K_t,Q,Gamma). Verified by a Python implementation and passing test showing a generated conflicting claim pair is correctly isolated (UndeterminedConflict, non-actionable) while a clean generated claim reaches DeterminedPositive/actionable.
